Total paid media spend in 2024 was $13,341,463.97. That covers the weeks whose Monday falls in 2024, filtered to paid channels.

Non-brand paid search spend in Q3 2025 was $1,308,446.91. That covers weeks whose Monday falls between 2025-07-01 and 2025-09-30, which is the first week starting 2025-07-07 through the week starting 2025-09-29.

{"answer": 1308446.91, "refused": false}

Brand-role channels took about 15.9% of 2025 paid media spend.

- Brand spend was $2,209,596.68 out of $13,905,118.46 total paid spend.
- The total is performance ($11,159,577.54), brand, and events ($535,944.24).
- I counted every channel flagged as paid, which includes events. If you'd rather exclude events, the share would be a bit higher.

{"answer": 15.89, "refused": false}

Paid Search Non-Brand had the highest paid spend in 2023, at about $3.60M. Paid Search Brand was next at about $2.40M.

{"answer": "Paid Search Non-Brand", "refused": false}

Connected TV spend in US Texas in 2024 was $162,081.69.

{"answer": 162081.69, "refused": false}

Meta had 50,843,074 impressions in the first half of 2025. That covers the weeks whose Monday falls between 2025-01-01 and 2025-06-30.

{"answer": 50843074, "refused": false}

LinkedIn's 2024 click-through rate was about 0.60%. That is 179,615 clicks divided by 29,819,086 impressions, which comes to 0.6024%.

{"answer": 0.6, "refused": false}

Non-brand paid search CPC in Q2 2024 was $7.07. That is $1,095,806 of spend over 154,930 clicks.

{"answer": 7.07, "refused": false}

YouTube's CPM in 2023 was $10.31. That's total YouTube spend per thousand impressions across all of 2023.

{"answer": 10.31, "refused": false}

Meta reported 56,233 conversions on its own platform in 2025. This is Meta's own claimed count, so it can overlap with other channels and overstate real leads.

{"answer": 56233, "refused": false}

Fernhook got 64,374 leads in Q1 2025. That counts the weeks whose Monday falls in the quarter, which runs from the week of 2025-01-06 to the week of 2025-03-31. The week of 2024-12-30 is excluded because its Monday is in Q4 2024.

{"answer": 64374, "refused": false}

Organic Search generated 42,762 leads in 2024. That is the last-touch source of new CRM leads, counted by the week each lead was created, for weeks starting 2024-01-01 through 2024-12-31.

{"answer": 42762, "refused": false}

We got 14,057 MQLs in March 2025. That counts weeks whose Monday falls in March, and each MQL is counted in the week it qualified.

{"answer": 14057, "refused": false}

Fernhook created 9,237 opportunities in Q2 2024. That counts the weeks whose Monday falls between 2024-04-01 and 2024-06-30.

{"answer": 9237, "refused": false}

In 2023 we created $93,237,550 in pipeline. That is the opportunity amount, counted in the week each opportunity was created, for weeks whose Monday falls in 2023.

{"answer": 93237550, "refused": false}

We had 10,445 closed-won deals in 2025, counting weeks whose Monday falls in 2025. The data notes say the latest weeks undercount deals because recent leads haven't had time to close, so the true total may be slightly higher.

{"answer": 10445, "refused": false}

Closed-won revenue in Q4 2024 was $7,495,830. That is the first-year contract value of deals won in weeks whose Monday falls between 2024-10-01 and 2024-12-31.

{"answer": 7495830, "refused": false}

Our 2024 win rate was 32.84%. That is 11,336 closed-won deals out of 34,518 closed deals (the 11,336 wins plus 23,182 losses).

{"answer": 32.84, "refused": false}

Meta's MQL rate for 2024 was 45.86%. That comes from 7,444 MQLs divided by 16,232 leads, using last-touch source. The metric is on an event-week basis, not a cohort rate. That means MQLs are counted in the week they qualified and leads in the week they were created.

{"answer": 45.86, "refused": false}

The EMEA sales area had 1,435 closed-won deals in 2025. That counts weeks whose Monday falls in 2025. The latest weeks undercount deals because recent leads haven't had time to close, so the true figure may be a little higher.

{"answer": 1435, "refused": false}

US Texas had the most closed-won deals in 2024, with 1,220. US California was second with 1,042.

{"answer": "US Texas", "refused": false}

Blended CPA for 2023 was about $1,292.49. That is $14,588,346.63 of paid media spend divided by 11,287 closed-won deals.

{"answer": 1292.49, "refused": false}

Brand paid search had a last-touch cost per lead of about $59.17 in 2025. That's spend divided by leads credited to Paid Search Brand as the last-touch source.

{"answer": 59.17, "refused": false}

YouTube's last-touch CPA in 2024 was about $14,235. That is its 2024 spend divided by the deals the CRM credits to YouTube as the last touch.

{"answer": 14235.24, "refused": false}

Blended cost per lead in Q4 2025 was about $53.91. That is $2,817,516.84 of paid spend divided by 52,266 leads. Blended CPL counts all leads, including those from unpaid sources, so it is lower than the CPL of paid channels alone.

{"answer": 53.91, "refused": false}

LinkedIn generated about $2.83 of pipeline per dollar of spend in 2023, on a last-touch basis. This is the governed `pipeline_per_dollar` metric for LinkedIn, covering weeks starting 2023-01-02 through 2023-12-25.

{"answer": 2.83, "refused": false}

Combined last-touch CPL for brand and non-brand paid search in 2024 was about $81.58. That is total spend of $6,473,459.20 divided by 79,351 leads.

| Channel | Spend | Leads | CPL |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paid Search Brand | $2,416,286.32 | 43,177 | $55.96 |
| Paid Search Non-Brand | $4,057,172.88 | 36,174 | $112.16 |

I pooled spend and leads rather than averaging the two channel CPLs, which would have given a different number.

{"answer": 81.58, "refused": false}

Total paid media spend in the week starting 2025-06-02 was $276,758.74.

{"answer": 276758.74, "refused": false}

YouTube had spend in 31 of the 53 weeks whose Monday falls in 2024. The other 22 weeks show zero spend.

{"answer": 31, "refused": false}

We sent 6,733,247 marketing emails in 2025. That counts the weeks whose Monday falls in 2025.

{"answer": 6733247, "refused": false}

The email open rate in 2024 was 29.17% (unique opens divided by emails sent, across weeks whose Monday falls in 2024).

{"answer": 29.17, "refused": false}

There were 64 AEs across all regions in the last week of 2024, which is the week starting 2024-12-30.

{"answer": 64, "refused": false}

We had 54 SDRs across all regions in the last week of June 2024, which is the week starting Monday 2024-06-24.

{"answer": 54, "refused": false}

The average weekly fleet activity index in 2025 was about 100.67. A value of 100 is typical, so 2025 was slightly above typical market demand.

{"answer": 100.67, "refused": false}

I can't give you a churn rate for 2025. The governed metrics don't include churn, retention, cancellations, or customer counts. The closest are closed-won and closed-lost deals, but those track new sales, not customers leaving. I'd have to invent a definition to estimate churn from them, so I haven't.

{"answer": null, "refused": true}

There is no NPS metric defined, and no customer satisfaction or survey data either. I can't answer this with the governed metrics, and I won't estimate it.

{"answer": null, "refused": true}

I can't answer this one. The governed metrics only break down by channel, channel group, marketing role, paid or unpaid, region and sales area. There is no campaign dimension, so I can't compare individual Meta campaigns on cost per lead. I could give you Meta's cost per lead for 2024 at the channel level, or split it by region, but that wouldn't answer which campaign was best.

{"answer": null, "refused": true}

I can't answer this. The governed metrics have no gross margin metric. They don't include cost of goods sold or any other cost or profit figures. The only revenue measure is closed-won revenue, which is first-year contract value. The only cost measure is paid media spend. Neither one gives gross margin. Calculating it from them would mean making up a definition.

{"answer": null, "refused": true}

I can't answer this with the governed metrics. Closed-won deals can only be broken down by channel, channel group, marketing role, paid status, region and sales area. None of the metrics or dimensions covers fleet size or vehicle count, so I can't filter deals to fleets with more than 100 vehicles. I haven't estimated a figure.

{"answer": null, "refused": true}

Fernhook's data has no TikTok channel, so I can't give you a TikTok CPA. The nine paid channels in 2025 are Paid Search Brand, Paid Search Non-Brand, Webinars, Connected TV, Display Retargeting, Affiliates and Partners, Meta, LinkedIn and YouTube. A TikTok query returned no rows. I haven't estimated the figure or mapped it to another channel, such as Meta or YouTube.

{"answer": null, "refused": true}
